description: Is the agent pool the bottleneck, how many CD attempts a version needs, and which tests keep failing. Replaces Agents and peak load, Release stability and Tests.

panels.title: Agents: is the pool the bottleneck?

panels.description: Daily peak busy agents (distinct agents) and the worst and 90th-percentile queue waits of jobs queued that day (the median is almost always 0 s and hides the tail). Symmetric-log scaling preserves zero-second medians; immediate assignments are included. PoolMaintenance is excluded. Observed load does not establish pool capacity. Dashed red line = busy agents at which jobs start to queue; set it with the "Queue starts at" box at the top (default 5 = pool size minus one for a 6-agent pool; use the pool size minus one for other pools).

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentLoadTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and Minute ge ${__from:date:iso} and Minute lt ${__to:date:iso})/groupby((Minute),aggregate(BusyAgents with sum as BusyAgents))&$top=100000

ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentJobsTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and QueuedAt ge ${__from:date:iso} and QueuedAt lt ${__to:date:iso} and Pipeline ne 'PoolMaintenance')/groupby((RequestId,QueuedAt,WaitSeconds))&$top=20000

panels.title: Peak agents vs queue wait per day

panels.description: The correlation itself: every hour of the range is grouped by how many agents were busy at its peak (x). Bars are the average hourly 90th-percentile wait (the median is almost always 0 s) and the worst queue wait of jobs queued in those hours (log). Waits that only climb at the right end = not enough agents; waits already high on the left = something other than capacity.

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentLoadTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and Minute ge ${__from:date:iso} and Minute lt ${__to:date:iso})/groupby((Minute),aggregate(BusyAgents with sum as BusyAgents))&$top=100000

ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentJobsTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and QueuedAt ge ${__from:date:iso} and QueuedAt lt ${__to:date:iso} and Pipeline ne 'PoolMaintenance')/groupby((RequestId,QueuedAt,WaitSeconds))&$top=20000

panels.title: Queue wait by pool load

panels.description: Where agent shortage hurts: total and worst queue wait per pipeline (PoolMaintenance excluded). Median waits are almost always 0 s, so look at the share of jobs that waited more than 60 s.

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentJobsTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and QueuedAt ge ${__from:date:iso} and QueuedAt lt ${__to:date:iso} and Pipeline ne 'PoolMaintenance')/groupby((Pipeline),aggregate(WaitSeconds with sum as Total,WaitSeconds with max as Worst,RequestId with countdistinct as Jobs))&$top=20000

ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentJobsTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and QueuedAt ge ${__from:date:iso} and QueuedAt lt ${__to:date:iso} and Pipeline ne 'PoolMaintenance' and WaitSeconds gt 60)/groupby((Pipeline),aggregate(RequestId with countdistinct as Over60))&$top=20000

panels.title: Pipelines by queue wait

panels.description: Busy time per agent. A few agents doing most of the work, or idle agents, show pool imbalance (capabilities/demands).

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentJobsTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and AssignedAt ge ${__from:date:iso} and AssignedAt lt ${__to:date:iso})/groupby((Agent,Pool),aggregate(BusySeconds with sum as Busy,RequestId with countdistinct as Jobs,BusySeconds with max as Longest))&$top=20000

Releases: how many CD attempts does a version need?

panels.description: Tests ranked by number of builds they failed in. Failing for = days since the first failure in the current streak (red over 7 days = broken, not flaky).

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOTestFailuresTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote})) and FailedAt ge ${__from:date:iso} and FailedAt lt ${__to:date:iso})/groupby((Test,Pipeline),aggregate(BuildId with countdistinct as Builds,FailingDays with max as FailingFor,FailedAt with max as Last))&$orderby=Builds desc&$top=100

panels.title: Most failing tests

panels.description: Per day and pipeline: failed / total tests over all test runs that finished that day (one line per pipeline). A floor that never reaches 0 = permanently broken tests; spikes = environment problems.

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOTestRunsTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Project:singlequote}) or Project in (${Project:singlequote})) and FinishedAt ge ${__from:date:iso} and FinishedAt lt ${__to:date:iso} and TotalTests gt 0)/groupby((TestRunId,Pipeline,FinishedAt,FailedTests,TotalTests))&$top=20000

panels.title: Test failure rate per day

panels.description: Peak busy agents per UTC weekday/hour across the selected range. Hours 0-23 use seven weekday rows and narrow hourly columns. The shared zero-based green/yellow/red scale shows relative observed load, not assumed capacity or failure thresholds.

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentLoadTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and ('__all' in (${Pool:singlequote}) or Pool in (${Pool:singlequote})) and Minute ge ${__from:date:iso} and Minute lt ${__to:date:iso})/groupby((Minute),aggregate(BusyAgents with sum as BusyAgents))&$top=100000

panels.title: Peak busy agents by weekday/hour (UTC)

panels.description: Busy agent hours per week, stacked by line. Weeks start on Monday (UTC). Agent hours = minutes in which an agent was busy on a job of that line, divided by 60 (a job counts from assignment to finish). The line is the one of the run the job belongs to: PR runs by target branch, CI runs by source branch. 'CD / Publish' are CD and Publish runs, which belong to environments, not lines. 'No run' are jobs without a run in the data (for example pool maintenance). Agents are shared by all lines. Note: most agent time sits in builds already purged from Azure DevOps; it is labelled by pipeline type (PR/CI/CD run no longer in Azure DevOps) instead of by line. Replaces the run-time-per-week chart: it comes from agent-job events, which outlive the builds, so it covers the whole period. Jobs of builds already purged from Azure DevOps are labelled by pipeline type.

targets.oDataQueryString: ADOTelemetry.ADOAgentLoadByLineTyped?$apply=filter(('__all' in (${Organization:singlequote}) or Organization in (${Organization:singlequote})) and Minute ge ${__from} and Minute lt ${__to})/groupby((Minute,Line),aggregate(BusyAgents with sum as Busy))&$top=100000

'No run' are jobs without a run in the data (for example pool maintenance). Agents are shared by all lines. Note: most agent time sits in builds already purged from Azure DevOps; it is labelled by pipeline type (PR/CI/CD run no longer in Azure DevOps) instead of by line.
